description: Conflict originally identified because Chapter 3 §1.1 states that modal auxiliaries use one present-tense form with all subjects and do not take a third-person-singular -s ending, while the original wording of AGR-002 generalized present-tense agreement to all verbs. Resolved by narrowing AGR-002 to present-tense non-modal verbs and adding the modal exception with examples and a Chapter 3 source.
proposed_resolution: RESOLVED with explicit human approval on 2026-11-05: AGR-002 now excludes modal auxiliaries from present-tense subject-verb agreement and cites Chapter 3 §1.1, p. 75. The new MORPH-006 rule records the invariant modal form.
